mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1.5% consistently signals accommodative monetary policy that compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS <= 1.5% occurs in 60% of cases but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate exceeding 4.5% signals economic weakness that triggers equity sell-offs due to reduced consumer spending confidence, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 4.5% occurs in 60% of cases but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous inflation acceleration (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) and low policy rates (FEDFUNDS < 1.5%) signal imminent aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS < 1.5%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion (HOUST > 1200), housing market strength signals economic overheating and potential policy tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST > 1200 occurs in 60% of cases but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 105) within the past month signals an imminent manufacturing contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 105 occurs in 60% of cases but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4.0%) over the past 3 months indicates a tight labor market that fuels consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE < 4.0% occurs in 60% of cases but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rising consumer spending (RSAFS > 1% MoM) and declining housing starts (HOUST < 1200) indicate consumption diversification away from housing, reducing bubble risks and supporting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where RSAFS > 1% MoM and HOUST < 1200, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent growth in consumer spending (RSAFS rising MoM > 0.5%) signals strong economic activity that supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS rising MoM > 0.5% occurs in 60% of cases but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of those instances.
